extractedText: Retail Investors Dump Samsung, SK hynix in First Selloff Since AprilIndividuals Sold 5.2 Trillion Won of Samsung Electronics, 7.8 Trillion Won of SK hynix Reversal Follows Four Straight Months of Net Buying From May Through August Foreign Investors Also Sold 3.9 Trillion Won, Adding to Supply Pressure Corporate Buyers Purchasing Treasury Shares Absorbed 14.5 Trillion WonFinance|Published 2026.09.13. 11:30:08|By Shin Ji-minjimnn@sedaily.com|Summary|SaveAAASamsung Electronics and SK Hynix. Yonhap NewsRetail investors who had been aggressively accumulating Samsung Electronics (005930.KS) and SK hynix (000660.KS) turned net sellers in September for the first time in five months. With foreign investors also continuing to sell, share buybacks by the two chipmakers absorbed the supply and supported the downside in their stock prices.Analysts say a strategy of raising exposure to semiconductors remains valid as the memory chip cycle continues to improve. Some caution, however, that whether expanded artificial intelligence investment translates into actual productivity gains and cash generation is the key variable for a longer-term rally.According to the Korea Exchange on the 13th, individual investors sold a net 5.21 trillion won ($3.7 billion) of Samsung Electronics and 7.82 trillion won ($5.6 billion) of SK hynix between Sept. 1 and Sept. 11. That amounts to more than 13 trillion won of selling in the two stocks alone.Individuals had bought both stocks for four consecutive months from May through August. Net purchases of Samsung Electronics rose from 9.61 trillion won in May to 17.12 trillion won in June, then fell to 5.05 trillion won in July and 2.04 trillion won in August. Net buying of SK hynix also topped 15 trillion won in both May and June before weakening rapidly to 9.01 trillion won in July and 1.07 trillion won in August. This month, both stocks flipped to net selling.Expectations for the chip cycle have not soured. OpenAI's unveiling of a new AI model called Astra revived hopes that broader AI adoption will lift demand for servers and memory. Even so, individuals moved to lock in profits as the KOSPI lost upward momentum in the third quarter and as overhead supply built up through the sharp selloff in June and July. Tighter rules on single-stock leveraged exchange-traded funds tracking Samsung Electronics and SK hynix are also cited as having damped some investment demand.Traders work at the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) in the U.S. Reuters-Yonhap NewsAlongside a decline in the won-dollar exchange rate, money also rotated out of domestic chip stocks and into U.S. technology shares. According to the Korea Securities Depository, domestic investors bought a net $73.26 million (about 98.6 billion won) of Alphabet, $65.22 million (87.7 billion won) of Broadcom and $54.09 million (72.8 billion won) of Meta this month. All three ranked among the 10 most-bought overseas stocks.Foreign flows are another burden. Through the 11th this month, foreign investors sold a net 1.96 trillion won each of Samsung Electronics and SK hynix, extending five straight months of net selling in the two stocks since May.While individuals and foreigners both dumped the two chipmakers, other corporate entities buying treasury shares absorbed the supply. Their net purchases this month reached 4.66 trillion won for Samsung Electronics and 9.89 trillion won for SK hynix. Because corporate buying was relatively larger for SK hynix, its shares gained 8.24% through the 11th this month. Samsung Electronics fell 0.19% over the same period.Analysts largely agree that the memory market itself remains solid regardless of near-term supply pressure. According to Hana Securities, average daily memory chip exports in August rose 271% from a year earlier to $1.58 billion, with DRAM and NAND exports up 473% and 322%, respectively. Kim Rok-ho, an analyst at Hana Securities, said sustained gains in memory prices are the foundation of the share price recovery.Some analysts, however, say expanded AI investment alone is not enough to guarantee a long-term rally in chip stocks. Kyobo Securities said the next question is whether Big Tech can recoup its increased capital spending through revenue and cash flow from AI businesses. Choi Bo-young, a research fellow at Kyobo Securities, said the condition for a long rally is a structure in which both the companies building AI and the companies using it make money.#SamsungElectronics#SKhynix#KOSPI#MemoryChips#RetailInvestors#KoreaStocksOriginal reporting by Shin Ji-min for Seoul Economic Daily.AI-translated from Korean.
